claim.quote: The combination with the corresponding measurement performed with data collected by the CMS experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV leads to an observed significance of 5.9 standard deviations, equal to the expected significance.

date.note: arXiv preprint submitted 1 August 2017 (v1); published as Phys. Lett. B 779 (2018) 283.

name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to tau leptons

significance.quote: an observed significance of 5.9 standard deviations
significance.value: 5.9σ observed (5.9σ expected), 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV data

summary.plain: CMS reports the first observation of Higgs boson decays to tau leptons by a single experiment, from 13 TeV data combined with earlier 7 and 8 TeV data (observed significance 5.9 standard deviations). Tau leptons are heavy relatives of the electron.
summary.technical: 35.9 fb^-1 at 13 TeV: H → ττ signal established with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations (4.7 expected), best-fit signal strength 1.09 +0.27/−0.26 times the standard model expectation; combined with 7 and 8 TeV data, observed significance 5.9 standard deviations, equal to the expected significance.

title: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons with the CMS detector
why_it_matters: The paper says that to establish the mass generation mechanism for fermions it is necessary to probe the direct coupling of the Higgs boson to such particles, and that H → ττ is the most promising decay channel because of the large expected event rate compared with the muon-pair channel and the smaller background than in the bb̄ channel.
